identity_evidence.quote: We present a case of fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and mesenteric ischemia in a 78-year-old woman with recurrent stage IIIC1 cervical cancer treated with pembrolizumab.

attribution_limitations: Printed reference-range units are inconsistent with the measured quantity (serum creatinine range in mg/mL against a value in mg/dL; blood glucose range in mEq/l; arterial pH range in ng/mL). The source text is kept literally and no unit is corrected or inferred.

The source says DKA likely contributed to mesenteric ischemia and shows a possible mechanism in Figure 4; this is hedged author interpretation and is not recorded as an established cause. Pembrolizumab causation of fulminant T1DM is likewise not stated as proven, only that T1DM developed after a single dose.

"On the following day" names no anchor; the adjacent preceding sentence is the anti-GAD confirmation ("Later, ..."), so the timeline orders it only by that adjacency and does not state which day it follows. Drowsiness, GCS 13 and blood glucose 873 mg/dL take that time because their sentence directly follows and describes the deterioration. Arterial pH 7.13, mechanical ventilation, the bleeding, both hemoglobin values, endoscopy and CT carry no stated time; they are ordered after the day-34 presentation only as in-hospital care, not dated to the following day.

Hemoglobin is stated only as a decrease from 9.9 g/dL to 7.7 g/dL: the order of the two values is stated, but neither has a time, and the 9.9 g/dL value is not placed relative to the day-34 presentation.

Surgical resection is named as the definitive treatment for intestinal necrosis but was not done because her general condition was too compromised; the source does not say surgery was ordered or scheduled, so it is recorded as not performed (assertion absent, action unknown), not as a cancelled order.
